attempted_claim: Prove or disprove the following mesoscopic two-point law: for Aztec diamonds of order N with N-dependent two-periodic weights (1,1,1,a_N) where a_N = 1 - gamma N^{-1/2} for fixed gamma > 0, so that the central smooth-diamond width and the smooth-phase correlation length are both of mesoscopic order, the covariance of the height function at two faces separated by a mesoscopic distance of order N^{1/2} within the crossover region converges to an explicit closed-form limiting kernel obtained from the product of the mesoscopic inverse-Kasteleyn asymptotics (equivalently, the conjectured massive/sine-Gordon two-point function with explicit mass determined by gamma); parameter scope is every fixed gamma > 0 and all fixed mesoscopic offsets in the crossover window; a complete answer is a rigorous derivation of the stated explicit limiting covariance for all such gamma and offsets, or a rigorous disproof by computing a different limit, proving gamma-dependence of a different form, or proving no such limit exists.
decisive_failure: No uniform mesoscopic inverse-Kasteleyn asymptotics for the N-dependent pinching spectral curve were established; the toy 1D computation illustrates but does not replace Aztec estimates; neither proof nor disproof of the mesoscopic covariance law was obtained, and the sine-Gordon identification step remains conjectural.
